question: Can an AI coach get you to a sub-3 marathon?
title: Can an AI coach get you to a sub-3 marathon? One runner is testing it
description: Not proven yet. I'm the test: five AI coaches plan my training for a sub-3 marathon at Chicago on October 10, 2027, and every real Garmin number goes up here, the bad ones too.
answer: Not proven yet. I'm the test. Five AI coaches plan my running, lifting, food and recovery for a sub-3 marathon at Chicago on October 10, 2027, and every number goes up here as it comes in, including the ones I'd rather hide.
On {start_date_long}, my Garmin said I'd run a {start_marathon} marathon. On {now_date_long}, it said {now_marathon}. Chicago asks for 2:59:59.

sections.h2: Where I am, from my Garmin
paras: Threshold pace is about the fastest pace I can hold for an hour, measured by my Garmin with a chest strap. I've been faster than I am today. That's a big part of why I think the gap can close.

Kai, the running coach, builds every week from the marathon research and my Garmin data. Speed comes first, for a 5K and then a 10K, before the half marathon and Chicago. The plan climbs from about {week_plan_miles} miles a week now to about 90 in August 2027, with hills every week.
Rook, the head coach, settles it when the others want different things from the same week. Pain I report goes on top, then the race. Every change gets written down with the rule behind it.

sections.h2: How you'll know if it worked
paras: The test has checkpoints: a 5K on December 26, another on February 7, 2027, a 10K on May 15 and a half marathon on September 5. Then Chicago. Each result goes on this site with the official time. If the coaching falls short, that goes up here too.

question: How do my AI coaches fit running and lifting together?
title: Running and lifting in one week: how my AI coaches keep them from colliding
description: Two of my five AI coaches share one week: one has the runs, one has the lifts. Heavy leg work goes on the hard-run days, hours after the run, and never the day before a hard run or the long run.
answer: Kai plans the runs, Bo plans three short lifts a week, and Rook, the head coach, decides when they collide. The rule that settles most fights: heavy leg work goes on the hard-run days, hours after the run, never the day before one.
I'm training for a sub-3 marathon at Chicago on October 10, 2027. This is what my week actually looks like right now.

sections.h2: My week, running and lifting together
table: Heavy lower body, sets of three
Upper body, kept light enough to hold
No legs: the long run is next
paras: Each lift is short, about 40 to 45 minutes, and always hours after that day's run.

sections.h2: How the coaches settle a clash
paras: Bo wants my legs strong. Kai wants them fresh for the hard days. When they disagree, Rook decides in the same order every time: pain I report first, then the marathon, then my weight, then strength. So the run usually wins, and Bo takes it better than you'd think.
Lower-body days land on the hard-run days, after the run, so my legs get a full day or more before the next hard effort. Saturday stays free of leg work before the Sunday long run.
It's one dad's week, drawn as a series. Every week of it goes into the Sunday letter. It isn't medical advice, and the coaches are AI characters.

question: What do my AI coaches watch when a runner starts at 258 lb?
title: Training for a marathon from 258 lb: what my AI coaches watch
description: I started training for a sub-3 marathon at 258 lb. Here is what my AI coaches watch for me: easy runs by heart rate, a foot check every morning, and eating enough to run.
answer: I started this at 258 lb, chasing a sub-3 marathon at Chicago in October 2027. My coaches don't treat my size as a reason to shrink the goal. They treat it as a reason to watch a few things closely: how hard my easy runs really are, how my feet feel at first light, and whether I'm eating enough to do the work.
This is one heavier runner's setup, not medical advice.

table: A heart-rate range learned from my own easy runs (109 to 120 bpm right now)
Pace alone would push me too hard on easy days
A 0 to 10 check each morning, first steps out of bed
Pain I report goes to the top of the board and can change that day's run
No more than about 2 lb a week, eating to hunger
Logged for miles, left out of my pace readings
Pushing a jogging stroller up a hill makes pace meaningless

sections.h2: What hasn't changed because of my weight
paras: The goal. Speed comes first, a 5K in February and a 10K in May, then marathon training with hills every week and about 90 miles a week at the peak in August 2027. The numbers on this site will show whether a runner my size can carry that.
